domains.title: Flow control and resilient services
domains.depth: Implementation, failure investigation, resource accounting and independent transfer

subtopics.title: Cancellation trees and budgets across clock domains

objectives.text: Derive deadline versus timeout semantics, cancellation precedence, parent lifetime and nonextension of inherited budget. Distinguish stopping admission from acknowledgement and rollback.

Implement checked scope construction and cross-clock remaining-budget encoding, including zero budget, numeric horizon, depth exhaustion and stale parent-lifetime counterexamples without executing invalid access.

Enumerate cancellation/expiry/finish orderings and verify output preservation, no later child deadline, idempotent cancellation and delayed borrower cleanup. Inject a completion after cancellation and retain its state until acknowledgement.

Transfer to an RPC chain with queued transport delay and independent clocks. Quantify which latency assumptions bound end-to-end completion and show why repeated per-hop timeout resets or copying an absolute monotonic timestamp violate the intended budget.

subtopics.title: Five overload policies and bounded pending producers

objectives.text: Specify each policy in terms of observable loss, ordering, caller ownership and completion; distinguish application admission, transport buffering and receiver consumption.
Implement all five policies, closed draining and the real channel adapter, including exactly-once transfer and explicit retained pending state.

Implement a two-producer readiness/cancellation adapter and falsify missed-wakeup, double-transfer and unbounded-pending assumptions with controlled event traces; bound queue plus producer-held memory together. Add explicit credit messages: start with four credits, consume one on admission, return one only when receiver capacity is released, and reject duplicate/stale credit returns so granted minus consumed plus returned never exceeds actual capacity.

Compare block/reject/drop/overwrite/degrade under an identical synthetic producer/consumer schedule, measuring accepted, lost, coalesced, queued and pending work separately. Transfer to owned payloads with a disposer and prove exactly-once cleanup on every rejected or discarded path.

subtopics.title: Hashed timer-wheel collisions, cancellation and expiry work

objectives.text: Derive bucket index, full due identity, list invariants and generation retirement. Prove why modulo bucket equality alone is insufficient across revolutions.
Implement bounded schedule/cancel/tick and a two-level cascade extension with no lost or duplicate expiries, explicit horizon, late tick and immediate timer policies.
Enumerate delays1..16, cancellation/reuse traces and same-bucket collisions against an ordered due-event oracle; test numeric exhaustion and every link removal position.

Compare heap, ordered list and wheel using equivalent ordering, horizon and cancellation guarantees. Measure worst expiry burst, empty-tick work, memory and jitter; distinguish per-timer output cost from constant bookkeeping claims.

subtopics.title: Overflow-safe token buckets and competing rate contracts

objectives.text: Derive the burst-plus-rate admission bound, initial credit, dimensional units and distinction between a policer, shaper, peak limit and concurrency limit.
Implement overflow-safe lazy refill and fixed-point fractional credit, specifying rounding, numeric horizon and which state changes persist on a rejected spend.

Exhaust small capacities/rates/time jumps against arbitrary-precision arithmetic and adversarial boundary costs; verify cumulative admitted cost bounds and kill free-refill/equality-rejection mutants.

Compose average and peak limits with atomic admission across both budgets. Compare token bucket and fixed/sliding windows under the same burst policy, and identify when different results arise from different contracts rather than implementation quality.

subtopics.title: Jittered retry schedules with a shared deadline and attempt budget

objectives.text: Derive bounded exponential windows, count the original attempt separately and explain why nested retries multiply work. Classify retryable outcomes without treating timeout as absence of side effects.
Implement schedule, unbiased bounded PRNG adapter and actual fault-model dispatch with a common limiter, preserving ownership of outstanding attempts until completion.
Enumerate every allowed draw for windows2/4/8, deadlines at each boundary and all capped attempt histories; use fault traces where an effect commits but its acknowledgement is lost.

Compare no-jitter, full-jitter and a documented alternative under fixed seeds and equal retry/deadline budgets. Measure peak synchronized work as well as completion latency; transfer to correlated client seeds and expose why jitter is not a security or safety guarantee.

subtopics.title: Health breakers, bulkheads and stale completions

objectives.text: Derive distinct health and capacity invariants, permit ownership, epoch identity and neutral-versus-backend-failure classification; explain why a failure window is not a concurrency bound.
Implement bounded admission/completion with generation and epoch exhaustion, including late old-epoch results and four-tick cooldown overflow retirement.
Model every two-permit completion ordering, stale/duplicate completion and half-open race. Add and test a sliding-window policy with an independent recomputation of its retained observations.

Transfer to two tenants and heterogeneous request costs. Derive isolation guarantees, starvation tradeoffs and cancellation acknowledgement, then compare recovery latency and retained resources under equal admission policies.

subtopics.title: Hedged responses and ownership of losing work

objectives.text: Separate first response from first acceptable response, result commitment from quiescence, and cancellation request from completed losing work. State prerequisites for safe hedging of side effects.
Implement exactly one winner and separately owned attempt lifetimes, with expiry, late response, repeated completion and unstarted-attempt rejection.

Implement and verify a synchronized two-worker completion arbiter, exercising both simultaneous success orders and winner/cancellation/timeout races under a controlled scheduler plus sanitizer checks.

Measure tail latency and total backend work under explicit independent versus correlated delay models. Transfer to a slow loser that completes after the client abandons its wait; preserve cleanup and prevent a stale generation from completing a new request.

subtopics.title: Idempotent effects, finite deduplication and storage fencing

objectives.text: Derive request identity versus payload equality, finite retention, authentication assumption and monotonic fencing enforcement at the actual effect resource. Identify which failures make a result uncertain.
Implement atomic in-memory record/effect publication, original-response replay, parameter mismatch rejection, no live-record eviction and checked arithmetic.

Demonstrate harmless replay/stale-writer violations using original mutants, then add a journal recovery model with crash injection at every write/flush/commit boundary and independently recompute recovered effects.

Transfer to multiple clients, reordered messages, restarted token issuer and expired dedup entries. State durability, uniqueness and monotonicity assumptions necessary for each guarantee; reject claims of network exactly-once delivery from a local lookup table.

subtopics.title: Resilient telemetry admission, committed effects and draining

objectives.text: Derive a composition contract with admission, effect commit, reply availability, notification enqueue, delivery and cleanup as distinct events. Account for every retained buffer, timer, permit and borrowed owner.

Implement the bounded service anchor using actual conc.channel and all required local IPC/reactor/fault adapters; preserve exactly-once notification for a new retained request and explicit replay/expiry semantics.

Inject allocation/partial-I/O/timeout/reset/cancellation/late-completion faults across the integrated service, checking effect and notification accounting with an independent event-sourced oracle and all declared capacity bounds.

Run an independently designed workload with burst arrivals, long tails, correlated faults and slow consumers. Seal a composition decision, apply all13 cost dimensions, and explain changed results under different correctness contracts or clock assumptions.
